The apparent fatness of the solution space arises from topological defects in the constraint sampling manifold (e.g., collinear or redundant points), which create spurious local minima in the loss landscape that trap optimization at finite widths, whereas a defect-free sampling would reveal a rigid solution space with finite $N_c$.

The rigidity classification is an artifact of the optimization "temperature" (effective noise level); deterministic solvers (low T) are trapped in local minima making $N_c \to \infty$, while stochastic solvers (high T) can traverse barriers to find the rigid solution, implying the intrinsic rigidity is obscured by the optimizer's dynamics.

The perceived dimensionality $N_c(w)$ depends on the composition of the initial weight distribution relative to the basis functions of the rigid family; if the initial composition lacks alignment with the rigid subspace (e.g., wrong activation symmetries), the network cannot represent the solution even if capacity exists, leading to apparent fatness.
